ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.14929v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Speech tokenizers serve as speech front ends, encoding input speech signals into representations for downstream models, such as automatic speech recognition (ASR) systems and large audio-language models (LALMs). In this paper, we find that speech tokenizers are fragile at the semantic level: small perturbations can disrupt their semantic encoding process and consequently cause severe degradation in downstream ASR and LALM performance. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Scaffolding Self-Transduction with Alignment Attention Mask for Aligner-Encoder ASR
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.15087v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: End-to-end ASR systems must jointly solve speech- text alignment and token prediction from sequence-level super- vision. We study this problem in Aligner-Encoder ASR, where alignment is performed inside encoder self-attention and can thus be directly intervened on with an attention mask. We use forced alignment to build an attention mask that confines selected encoder self-attention heads to a narrow window around the alignment path. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.15362v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Semantic endpointing must distinguish a completed turn from a temporary pause, yet its binary output does not require the full generation pathway of an audio-language model. We propose JEV-VAD, an ASR-free framework that combines task-first conditioning, a scalar endpoint readout, and decoder-prefix pruning. The question and completion criteria are placed before audio tokens, allowing causal decoder attention to construct audio states conditioned on the endpointing objective. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: qVocalTract: Efficient encoding framework of vocal-tract spectra on a quantum computer
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.15919v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The vocal-tract transfer function links the physical articulatory model to speech. Quantum encoding of vocal-tract transfer functions requires circuits that preserve acoustic structure under hardware noise. This paper proposes the qVocalTract framework, which uses optimized, ancilla-free staircase layers for spectral loading. Simulations and a superconducting processor compare this approach with sequential matrix-product-state preparation on vocal-tract data. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.16371v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: We propose structured speaker conditioning (SSC) for diarization-guided target-speaker recognition. SSC combines local activity structure with session-level acoustic identity to construct identity-consistent target conditions that control the acoustic encoder. Target-centric relational encoding (TCRE) retains per-speaker activity histories and factorized second- and third-order relations, capturing overlap and turn changes with aggregation cost linear in the number of tracks. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.16637v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: The interaction of acoustic features in leaking private information remains underexplored. This work focuses on time-domain features, i.e., broadband RMS level and pitch, alone and combined with temporally smoothed and subsampled Mel spectrograms. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: MESH: Multi-receiver Evaluation of Spatial Hearing across Egocentric and Allocentric Views
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.16787v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Spatial hearing in multi-receiver environments requires identifying who speaks, where they are, and how they move. Existing benchmarks evaluate spatial prediction, transcription, tracking, and distributed speech processing, but offer limited evaluation of whether speech signal remains associated with the correct physical source across receivers and motion. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Kezek: Splitting Mono Two-Person Conversations into Per-Speaker Tracks for Full-Duplex Dialogue Data
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.16933v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Full-duplex spoken dialogue models learn turn-taking, overlaps and backchannels from conversations recorded with one channel per speaker, but most available conversational audio is a single mono mix. We present Kezek, a model that turns a mono recording of exactly two people into one track per person with the original length and timing; overlaps and short replies ("yeah", "mm-hm") stay on the track of the person who said them. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: An LLM Is All You Need: Data-Efficient Adaptation to Full-Duplex, Word-Level Spoken Dialogue
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.14774v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Full-duplex spoken dialogue, in which a system listens while it speaks and can backchannel, yield the floor, and be interrupted, is usually obtained by training on hundreds of thousands to millions of hours of speech. This is costly, rewrites the language model that supplies the system's knowledge, and still leaves turn-taking either implicit or decided coarsely rather than word by word. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.14801v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: BEST-RQ, based on random projection and quantization, has been a well-established self-supervised learning approach to learn speech representations from large-scale unlabeled audio due to its high performance and efficiency. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.14908v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: We present Hy ASR 3.0, a large language model (LLM)-based automatic speech recognition (ASR) system that delivers strong recognition accuracy, supports flexible contextual conditioning, and maintains robust recognition performance across diverse speech conditions. Hy ASR 3.0 supports Mandarin Chinese, English and 13 Chinese dialect groups, including Cantonese. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).title: Human-Likeness and Conversational Preference Diverge for Synthesized Agent Speech in Customer-Service Calls
ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.16051v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Listeners can judge an agent's speech on how human it sounds (human-likeness) and on how much they would want to talk to it (conversational preference). Listening tests rarely ask about conversational preference, so the relation between the two judgments is unclear. We compared them in paired-choice tests on 120 turns that actors improvised as customer-service representatives. On each trial, two agents spoke the same turn. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2611.16718v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Recent music foundation models have achieved remarkable progress in music representation learning, yet most existing approaches rely on Transformer architectures whose quadratic attention complexity introduces substantial computational and memory overhead when modeling long-duration music recordings. In this work, we propose MusicRWKV, a multimodal music representation learning framework built upon the RWKV architecture. ArXiv eess.AS (Audio).description:
arXiv:2603.27998v4 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Individualized head-related impulse responses (HRIRs) enable binaural rendering, but dense per-listener measurements are costly. We address HRIR spatial up-sampling from sparse per-listener measurements: given a few measured HRIRs for a listener, predict HRIRs at unmeasured target directions. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.14592v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Accurate future channel state information (CSI) is essential for underwater acoustic (UWA) communication because delays associated with signal propagation, feedback, scheduling, and transceiver reconfiguration can render currently available CSI outdated. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.14634v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Despite the increasing sophistication of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI), research on the evaluation of AI-generated musical creativity remains limited. To address this gap, this paper proposes a quantitative framework for the formalization and evaluation of AI musical creativity. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.14724v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Natural-language audio editing requires connecting a user's intent to specific sounds and time regions while preserving surrounding content. Complex requests make this connection demanding: an edit may select one occurrence, depend on a temporal relation, or modify a source that overlaps with other sounds. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.14971v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Existing studies have shown that music generative models can generate synchronized tracks that play alongside an input song. Can we extend this capability to develop a generative approach to beat tracking? ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.15242v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Raga recognition in Hindustani classical music is difficult because a raga is not defined only by the notes used in it. Its identity also depends on the way notes are emphasized, the movement between notes and characteristic phrases. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.15288v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Speaker representation learning is fundamental to speech processing tasks such as speaker verification and diarization. Although long-context speaker encoders can produce stable and discriminative embeddings, short-duration verification and diarization require finer-grained temporal representations. Abstract: Acoustic Anomaly Detection (AAD) serves as a non-contact approach for machine condition monitoring, yet much of the existing research is evaluated offline and rarely addresses embedded hardware constraints or microphone variations under operational drift. ArXiv cs.SD (Sound).description:
arXiv:2611.16525v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: ZONOS3-Mini is an ultra-compact, ultra-fast, zero-shot voice-cloning TTS model. The model can run in real time on a laptop or smartphone. For its latency and size, it achieves state-of-the-art accuracy and cloning fidelity. If today is a day to celebrate good things happening in the USA, you better also be listening to the epic collaboration between Jlin and Chicago's Third Coast Percussion. CDM — Create Digital Music.title: Mixxx could unlock free and open standalone DJing — but, like, stable
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
Daniel Schürmann of the long-running libre/free DJ software project Mixxx has a compelling proposal for uniting efforts to develop their DJ software on embedded hardware, from emerging cheap "open" hardware to DIY projects. It could mean a chance for openness to have a moment -- while avoiding the chaotic slop of countless separate forks and hacks.

CDM — Create Digital Music.title: The techno originator, Juan Atkins, has died at 64
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
It's a loss that's beyond words. Juan Atkins, who coined the term "techno" and is often called "the originator," has died at 64. My deepest condolences to friends, family, and so many people I know who worked with and were inspired by this singular human being.

CDM — Create Digital Music.title: sndstation will transform cheap gaming consoles into music handhelds
CDM — Create Digital Music.description:
Cheap handheld gaming consoles now often pack surprising processing power. But many risk ending up as e-waste. A new open-source project is turning them into powerful Linux music workstations, instead, complete with the ability to run plug-ins—and original games, too. Oh, and the project has some familiar faces involved. Here's an exclusive first look.
